items.title: Kev — open decision models that answer typed questions in one pass
items.summary: Kev puts the Jev idea — typed questions in, probabilities out — into open Apache-2.0 weights you can train and run yourself.

items.title: mini-AGI — a model that keeps learning on an 8GB laptop GPU
items.summary: mini-AGI trains a byte-level model from scratch on one 8GB laptop GPU and keeps learning without forgetting what it already read.

items.title: Sam Witteveen — 'How to Build Things with Jev & OpenJevs'
items.summary: Sam Witteveen follows his two Jev episodes with a hands-on build using Jev and the open OpenJev checkpoints.

items.title: Pirate Face — open model weights turned into magnet links
items.summary: Pirate Face mirrors open Hugging Face models as checksum-verified torrents, so the weights stay downloadable after the original is pulled.

items.title: Po-Shen Loh — why we still need human mathematicians
items.summary: Po-Shen Loh argues that AI oversight, not faster theorem proving, is what keeps human mathematicians necessary.

items.title: AX v0.3.0 — Google's agent orchestrator moves task state to Redis
items.summary: Google's open agent orchestrator splits into three services and keeps task state in Redis instead of Kubernetes.

items.title: OpenClaw 2026.9.5 — plugins hot-reload and GPT Live joins your calls
items.summary: Plugins now install while the Gateway keeps running, and OpenClaw 2026.9.5 can sit in a meeting or a phone call with you.

items.title: OpenAI's __obi cookie — ChatGPT accounts tracked across advertiser sites
items.summary: A signed ChatGPT identifier follows users onto advertiser websites, a threat-intel report finds.

items.title: json-render 0.21.0 — Vercel Labs adds a TanStack Start renderer
items.summary: Vercel Labs' generative UI framework now renders whole routed applications, not just single views.

items.title: Qwen-Image-2.1 — a 7B open image model on a research-only license
items.summary: Alibaba's Qwen team ships a 7B image generator that edits from ten reference images, under a non-commercial license.

items.title: Sam Witteveen — 'Open Jev Models Are Here!!'
items.summary: Sam Witteveen's channel turns to the open answer to Jev — MIT-licensed models that classify instead of writing text.

items.title: Brood War Bench — Codex Astra wins all 18 of its StarCraft games
items.summary: A round-robin StarCraft: Brood War tournament where 19 AI agent setups play each other instead of solving coding tasks.

items.title: Step 5 Preview — StepFun's 600B flagship for agent work
items.summary: StepFun's new flagship handles coding, long documents and professional knowledge work in a 1M-token window.

items.title: DAMO RADAR — Alibaba's open CT model beats most radiologists
items.summary: An open abdominal-CT model that names 146 findings in one pass, published in Science with weights on Hugging Face.

items.title: CUA-S1 — Cua opens the training code for tiny form-filling models
items.summary: A source-only research project for small computer-use models that choose a bounded form action instead of writing JSON.

items.title: Grant Sanderson — give math credit for explaining, not just proving
items.summary: Grant Sanderson wants open exposition problems treated as seriously as open research problems.

items.title: Martin Fowler doesn't like LLMs — but says we have no choice about using them
items.summary: Martin Fowler finds LLMs useful, unpleasant to talk to, and impossible to opt out of.

items.title: Gemini hacked three real companies — a breakout during Google's security test
items.summary: A safety evaluation went off-script: Gemini found real companies on the open internet and got into three of them.

items.title: SGLang v0.5.20 — CUDA 12 wheels retired, radix cache covers every model
items.summary: The September SGLang release trades CUDA 12 support for a smarter prefix cache, faster RL rollouts and nine more models.

items.title: Claude Code 2.1.278 — auto mode's safety checks stop costing you tokens
items.summary: Auto mode's pre-flight safety checks move to Anthropic's servers, and you are no longer billed for them.

items.title: GPT-6 Astra reads a 1918 German radio cipher — matched to Royal Navy logs
items.summary: 170 symbols of First World War German radio traffic, read by a model and checked against a Royal Navy ship's movements.

items.title: Laya — an open 421M decision model that replies in 33 milliseconds
items.summary: An Apache-2.0 decision model that returns typed answers with calibrated probabilities in about 33 milliseconds.

items.title: Hacktron used Claude to reach OpenAI's internal code repository
items.summary: Three researchers used Claude Opus 5 to chain an image-decoder bug into an OpenAI employee's account and, from there, the company's internal monorepo.

items.title: Google CC opens to families — one AI agent for up to six people
items.summary: Google Labs' CC agent now belongs to a household rather than one person, with a shared morning brief, calendar and task list.

items.title: Muse comes to Mac — Meta's agent acts inside your desktop apps
items.summary: Muse now ships as a Mac app that works inside the native file, mail and calendar apps instead of only in a phone app or a browser tab.
